summary: Excessive end-to-end latency followed by 504 on very long multi-part system+user prompts with large max_tokens
description: Customer reports repeated 504 Gateway Timeouts when invoking long multi-part prompts (system + multiple user chunks) with max_tokens set to a high value (>= 120k token budget). Requests begin streaming but stall mid-generation; client receives partial output then HTTP 504 after ~62-68s. Impacting several downstream jobs in production — note-taking export and large-context summarization pipelines are failing intermittently.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use the hosted API endpoint in us-east with a single request containing: a) a 20k token system prompt, b) three user message chunks totaling ~40k tokens. 2) Set max_tokens to 120000 and temperature 0.2. 3) Enable streaming and a client timeout at 70s. 4) Observe response initially streaming tokens then stall; connection closed by gateway returning 504 after ~65s.

investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: large multi-part system prompts are preventing effective KV prefix reuse and triggering repeated cache reloads, which increases per-token latency later in the run. Observed finalizer queue growth coincident with kernel swaps when sequence length grows past internal thresholds (~60k tokens). We also saw a regression in a recent kernel selection change (PR #2844) that altered kernel warm/cold swap timing; may be amplifying tail latency for very deep contexts. Notably this happens most often when streaming is enabled and client timeouts are aggressive (70s range).
Actions taken so far:
- Reproduced in staging with smaller datasets; confirmed latency spike occurs after repeated prefix reloads.
- Scoped to serving-runtime change in PR 2844; reverted kernel selection heuristics in a local build and saw reduced finalizer queue depth in tests.
- Confirmed that dedicated capacity route (customer_dedicated_pool) avoids the 504s at same payload sizes due to higher kernel residency and lower kernel swap rate.
Open questions: exact interaction between finalizer timeout config, KV reload frequency, and upstream gateway timeout; whether batching policy changes in PR 2844 reduced prioritize-for-low-latency options.

resolution: Workaround and temporary mitigations provided: 1) Recommend reducing max_tokens and/or splitting prompts into smaller chunks; 2) Route high-token-budget requests to Dedicated pools for customers on enterprise; 3) Customer applied client-side higher timeout (120s) as last resort. Engineering patch (GH #2851) proposed to adjust kernel residency heuristic and add a measured delay before aggressive kernel swap to avoid finalizer queue amplifications. Status: in progress; ETA for rollback or mitigations in prod: 2026-03-18. Follow-up action: include targeted e2e tests for deep-context scenarios in CI and create alert for finalizer queue growth tied to long-context requests.
